lines.vo: The U.S. Navy once delivered the mail... by guided missile.
June 8th, 1959. Off Florida, the submarine USS Barbero carries a Regulus missile.
Inside: three thousand letters. All from the Postmaster General.
More than a hundred miles to the Navy's air station at Mayport... in about twenty-two minutes.
The Postmaster General called it "of historic significance to the peoples of the entire world."
He also predicted: "Before man reaches the moon, mail will be delivered within hours... to England, to India or to Australia, by guided missiles."
Ten years later, man reached the moon.
And the earliest known U.S. rocket mail? 1936. Unofficial.
Two rockets, across a frozen lake.
Both crash-landed short and slid along the ice... so the Hewitt postmaster dragged the mailbags the rest of the way.
Would you have trusted a missile with your mail?
